title: Define a retention policy for completed-round device-test workflow.js scripts instead of letting run2/run3 accumulate in tool/ indefinitely
why: Each script hardcodes one specific device IP, throwaway test-account PINs, and references specific numbered fixes ('FIX#7', 'FIX#9') from one already-completed testing round (run2, run3). git history shows later rounds (run-6, run-7, per the repo's recent commit log) left no equivalent *.workflow.js files behind, so retention is inconsistent — a reader can't tell whether run2/run3 are kept deliberately as re-runnable regression scripts or are simply uncleaned leftovers, and there is no tool/README documenting either answer.
recommendation: Document a retention rule for run-N workflow scripts (e.g. archive completed rounds under docs/audits/ next to the bug-log report they produced, or delete once their fixes have landed and been verified), and apply it to run2/run3.
acceptance_criteria: tool/ (or a new tool/README) states the retention rule for *.workflow.js device-test scripts
run2/run3 scripts are archived, removed, or explicitly kept per that stated rule

corrections: A parallel, currently-active device-test script family (tool/device_e2e/run2_full_suite.mjs .. run7_full_suite.mjs, dated Jun23-29, root-level tool/) exists and effectively supersedes these; the finding missed it but its core claim (no documented retention policy for the old family) still stands.
